extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, librarians, and readers interested in children's and young adult literature and book awards
extracted.subtask_short: Horn Book Award eligibility and selection
extracted.subtask_description: A library subject-guide summary of the Boston Globe–Horn Book Awards explaining categories, eligibility, and the awards' selection process, with a list of recent winners. Useful for researchers or readers seeking bibliographic and award-eligibility information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are selected in three categories: Picture Book, Fiction and Poetry, and Nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists winners organized by year and category (examples provided for 2019–2025). Use the category definitions when determining which submissions/titles belong to which award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication eligibility (geographic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The winning titles must be published in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A title's eligibility is tied to U.S. publication; works published elsewhere are not eligible unless published in the U.S. within the eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator nationality allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles may be written or illustrated by citizens of any country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no citizenship restriction on authors or illustrators — eligibility depends on U.S. publication rather than author nationality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and judge appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards are chosen by an independent panel of three judges who are annually appointed by the editor in chief of the Horn Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges form an independent three-person panel; appointments are made each year by the Horn Book editor in chief. The awards are customarily announced in June and have been presented since 1967.
